News.title: Punter visits his 10,000th British boozer and celebrates with another pint
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SAME AGAIN?

SAME AGAIN? Punter visits his 10,000th British boozer and celebrates with another pint

A PUNTER aiming to visit every UK pub has shown he is well on track with a pint in his 10,000th boozer.

Dale Harvey has averaged about 200 venues a month for his challenge.



The former publican reached his milestone in Edinburgh but said he was 100 per cent determined to complete his challenge.

He launched The Great British Pub Crawl in 2022 — estimating there to be about 35,000 to get to.



He joked he was motivated by his wife, Holly, telling him he could not do it.

He said: “Any time my wife tells me I’ll never do something, that makes me ten times more determined to go through with it.”

Dale is having a break to go on holiday, but will be back on it when he returns.

He said his aim was also to promote pub culture and the financial pressures faced.

He said: “Here’s to the next 10,000.

“I’m certainly not going to stop.



“I’m not going to slow down.

“I’m going to carry on — while there are issues to highlight, I’ll be out there doing this.”

News.title: Brit man who found dream Spanish home on Channel 4’s A Place in the Sun fears wife is among 13 killed in wildfires
News.content:
'THEY HAD NO CHANCE'

'THEY HAD NO CHANCE' Brit man who found dream Spanish home on Channel 4’s A Place in the Sun fears wife is among 13 killed in wildfires

A BRIT man who survived the Spanish wildfires in a car said he watched his wife “walk out in front of the firewall” – and fears she had “no chance”.

Malcolm Timbrell’s home in Bédar was consumed by flames last Thursday evening, killing 13 people, as fires swept expat hotspots in Almería.



The 70-year-old expat and his wife Annette Kilgore, 69, had found the property on the Channel 4 programme A Place in the Sun.

He told the BBC: “You’d never imagine it could happen.



“And when it does, and you’re the only survivor, then you’re left in a situation of, ‘What can I do?'”

Bédar was at the epicentre of Thursday’s wildfire – one of the deadliest in Spanish history.



Malcolm, Annette and 12 of their friends had just seconds to flee.

As the inferno raced towards their hilltop home, the group decided to escape by car.

But Malcolm said he ran back for their cats Charlie and Lilly.

He told the outlet: “If we’d have done the sensible thing and gone the other way and let our cats die, we both would be alive.



“But when you’ve got animals, you don’t think like that.”

Once back outside the house with both cats, Malcolm described a chilling scene.

The group had stopped and were standing outside their vehicles.



“My wife and our other seven friends and neighbours – against me screaming at them not to – decided the only safe way was to walk out in front of the firewall”, he said.

Malcolm later heard the flames were ripping across the land at a terrifying 20km per hour. “They had no chance”, he said.

Now alone, Malcolm ran to the abandoned cars for safety from the oncoming blaze.

Four of the six cars instantly combusted, but he managed to survive huddled in “the last one with a cat”, he said.

Malcolm was rescued by emergency crews after the flames had passed – but the bodies of eight people were discovered on a nearby path.



Now he must wait for DNA results to confirm the identities of the bodies.

“After that, I will probably just fall apart”, he told the outlet.

Malcolm said he had an “amazing life” with Annette, his wife of 17-ears, who he described aas “happy” and “outgoing” person.



The wildfires have been some of the worst that Spain has ever seen – with more than 16,000 acres burned to the ground and 1,448 people evacuated.

Four bodies found in a burnt-out wreck of a car are also believed to be Brits.

The burnt-out shell of the Honda Accord had a steering wheel on the right-hand side and was discovered on a deadly “trap” route in Los Gallardos.

The total death toll rose to 13 after it was announced that a 93-year-old Brit pensioner died late on Saturday.

It comes as Brits caught up in the deadly blazes in southern Spain blasted authorities for giving “no warning”.



Spanish authorities have claimed many of the dead did not follow official advice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Survivor Bob Layton, originally from Birmingham, said he had lost friends in the tragedy.

He said he was “sick to the back teeth of hearing that people didn’t follow the ‘designated escape route” and claimed there was no warning given about the inferno.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe suspect ‘scoffed pizza at home just five hours after murder’ as terror cops dismiss ‘burglary gone wrong’
News.content:
TERROR police took charge of the Ann Widdecombe murder investigation as fears grew the brutal killing was politically motivated.

They said they were acting on evidence found as they re-arrested the prime suspect, in Rotherham, South Yorks, on suspicion of terrorism.



The prime suspect arrived home about five hours after Ann Widdecombe was killed — and scoffed a supermarket pizza.

The 28-year-old is believed to have made the 540-mile round trip to Devon, where the former Tory minister was bludgeoned to death, in one day.



He left home in Rotherham, South Yorks, at 7.51am on Wednesday — and his red Vauxhall Corsa was back on the driveway at 6pm.

The man, who lived alone in a red-brick council house, ate a Pizza Express Sloppy Giuseppe that night — but did not emerge from his home again for three days.

He came out only on Saturday morning to put rubbish in his wheelie bin, CCTV reveals.

The footage, taken just after 10am, showed him shirtless, wearing a pair of blue shorts and carrying a plastic bag.

He turned back, walked past his Corsa and called for his barking labradoodle, Rave, to come back inside with him.

Later that night, armed terror police stormed in and arrested him, leading him, still shirtless, out of the house in handcuffs.



The suspect’s movements are being pieced together by officers — as the investigation was passed to anti-terror police amid fears the murder was politically motivated.

Detectives believe 78-year-old Ann, who switched allegiance from the Tories to Reform, was killed at her bungalow in the remote village of Haytor at 12.30pm on Wednesday.

At first, officers thought she died in a fall and did not realise she was murdered until a day later.



Devon and Cornwall Police top brass repeatedly played down the idea of a political motive, fuelling speculation that it was a burglary that turned violent.

But in a dramatic twist yesterday, counter-terror police took over the murder investigation.

They say it followed the examination of electronic devices belonging to the suspect after he was taken into custody.

He was re-arrested on suspicion of “commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism”.

It suggests the plot to kill Ann, known for her forthright socially conservative views, was for political, ideological or religious reasons.



Terror suspects can be held without charge for up to 14 days instead of the standard 24 hours for other criminal matters.

Head of National Counter Terrorism Policing Laurence Taylor described it as “a dynamic and complex investigation”.

He added: “Building on the progress made by our colleagues in Devon and Cornwall Police, we now have new information and evidence that means Counter Terrorism Policing is now leading the investigation. We are pursuing multiple lines of inquiry to establish the motivation for this attack.



“Our priority is progressing this investigation quickly, with all the capabilities we have available to us.

“If anyone has any information, please share it with the police.

“We would like to thank local communities, the wider public and the media for their ongoing support and patience, and would ask them to continue to support us in the next stage of the investigation.”

The shift to counter-terror police appears to vindicate claims by Reform UK leader Nigel Farage it was a “premeditated murder”.

He refused to accept the killing was a burglary gone wrong — but was accused of exploiting Ann’s death for political propaganda.



Devon and Cornwall Chief Constable James Vaughan defended his force, saying it “mounted an extraordinary response to a horrific murder of a very prominent public figure”.

He said the “lightning pace” of the investigation had shown “British policing at its very best”.

Meanwhile, it emerged that a Ring doorbell camera fitted to the front doorframe of Ann’s home provided officers with the crucial breakthrough in the case.



The veteran politician was interviewed on TalkTV at 8am that morning — just as the suspect apparently set off from home.

Ann was due to appear on Channel 5’s Matt Allwright show at 1pm.

She replied to a text from a producer at 12.19pm but failed to join a Zoom link sent to her at 12.48pm.

Her body was found at about 11.40am the following day.

She sustained serious head injuries and was covered in blood.



The door camera caught images of a white British man and his car allowing counter-terror officers to use specialist resources to pinpoint the suspect’s address in the Kimberworth area of Rotherham.

Further CCTV obtained by The Sun showed police arriving to arrest the suspect just after 9pm on Saturday.

Two armed officers sprinted into the front garden with their weapons drawn as others followed behind.



The front and back of the property was secured before the shirtless suspect was led out in handcuffs.

He was placed in the back of a police van and taken to a nearby station.

Scenes of crime officers in white suits immediately entered the property to begin a meticulous search for evidence.



His red hatchback was towed away at 3am.

Officers also searched his bins and the bushes at his home.

Residents continued to leave floral tributes near Ann’s home amid shock over her murder.

Resident Wayne Maloney said: “After the news broke, people were pretty scared to go out because there was a killer on the loose.”

He added that there was relief when police made an arrest only for fears to return when that suspect was released.



He said: “When we had the second arrest, it was like ‘Thank goodness’.”

In Rotherham, neighbours said the suspect had lived at the property for several years with his engineer father.

They said his dad, who was an amputee, died in hospital just before Christmas.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His mum and two older brothers live nearby.

Residents described him as “polite and kind” saying he would often put out their bins. But he rarely went out and left his car on the driveway.

News.title: Former Spanish MP arrested after ‘touching himself in front of 50 tourists including kids at hotel pool’
News.content:
SICK ACT Former Spanish MP arrested after ‘touching himself in front of 50 tourists including kids at hotel pool’

A DISGRACED ex-politician who allegedly masturbated in front of children at a hotel pool has been arrested.

Pere Albo, 54, stands accused of exposing himself to around 50 holidaymakers including kids at a four-star resort in Costa Brava, Spain.



Witnesses said they saw the former MP and mayor lie on a lounger, pull down his trousers and “visibly touch himself”, according to local papers.

One young woman told police that the 54-year-old had grabbed her arm while pleasuring himself, claim reports in the Catalan press.



Some of the witnesses are then said to have tried to assault the alleged exhibitionist.

Horrified hotel staff called police on the suspected flasher at around 5:30pm yesterday.

Albo told local paper El Punt Avui he had been drinking before entering the hotel and falling asleep on a poolside lounger – only to be rudely awakened by the police.

He told the paper that he had gaps in his memory – and requested video evidence of the incident.

He added: “I will apologise, if necessary.”

Local reports said that the ex-left-wing politician seemed “unbalanced and out of his mind” at the time of his arrest.



Albo, who is also a lawyer and hotelier, spent the night in a jail cell but reportedly insisted that his arrest was “illegal” – a claim which was later dismissed.

Besides his discussions with reporters, the suspected sex fiend has yet to make an official comment about the alleged incident at Tahita Playa Hotel.

Albo started his career in politics in 2007 as mayor of Sant Feliu de Guixols for the Socialists’ Party of Catalonia.



He was then deputy-mayor of the same region between 2011 and 2015 before becoming an MP gunning for Catalonian independence from 2021 to 2024.

He abandoned front-line politics last year but remains a member of MESCat, a pro-independence party.

MESCat today issued a statement expressing its “absolute dismay and surprise” at Albo’s alleged flashing stunt before announcing an internal probe.

It also said it was suspending his party membership as a “precaution” until it had more information.

Court officials said he had been held under suspicion of “indecent exposure” in front of a minor.



Cops have launched a probe into Albo but the former mayor is now back on the streets after being released on bail.

News.title: Shocking moment mum, 35, driving Mercedes runs red light before smashing into police car sending it up in flames
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a 35-year-old mum ran a red light before smashing into a police car and sending it up in flames.

CCTV footage shows Stacie Wright’s white Mercedes-Benz A-Class plough into the squad car after she ignored a red light in Birkenhead, Merseyside.



Wright, 35, was seen on video beginning to turn right directly into the path of the police vehicle before the two collide.

Within seconds, flames can be seen erupting from beneath the bonnet of the police car.



Wright, of Rock Ferry, Merseyside, has now been handed an eight-month jail sentence, suspended for 12 months.

The mum was driving at around 11.15pm on November 12 when she crossed a junction despite the traffic lights having been red for up to eight seconds, Liverpool Crown Court heard.

At the same moment, a police car with its blue lights flashing was travelling through a green light on Watson Street.

The impact sparked an immediate fire in the front of the police car, a court heard.

Meanwhile the officer inside suffered injuries and was left traumatised by the crash.

The £15,000 police vehicle was destroyed in the crash and written off, with a further £2,500 in salvage costs.



In a victim personal statement read to the court, Constable Thompson described the aftermath.

He said: “I suffered cuts to my face and bruising, as well as tinnitus and pain to my ribs which took two months to heal.

“I’m struggling to sleep as I cannot get comfortable due to my injuries, causing difficulties with my relationship.



“The fact my vehicle was actually on fire was terrifying. Such is the burden on me to put others first, my first thought was to get out and check on the driver.

“Had I been going one or two miles per hour faster, I could have killed someone.

“How close I was to losing everything due to the actions of someone else.”

Constable Thompson continued: “Every time I close my eyes to go to sleep I still see the flames coming up the bonnet and the smoke filling up my lungs.

“My 12-year-old has additional needs and she is still recovering from being woken in the night to be told what had happened.



“Even six months on, she still makes passing remarks about the crash.”

The officer also said he had been left in “extreme pain”, had to take time off work and missed training opportunities, causing “financial difficulties”.

Defending, Mr Hunt said Wright, a “hardworking” single mother and hairdresser, was “genuinely remorseful” and described the collision as a “moment of inattention”.

Sentencing, Charles Wood, Head of the Bench, said the CCTV showed Wright had committed “the most serious offence” under the sentencing guidelines.

He said: “The CCTV footage is very clear, and having seen it we determine this is a category A1 offence, the most serious offence.



“The traffic light you went through was red for a significant period of time, as much as eight seconds. Clearly, a lot of inattention on your behalf.

“Nine times out of ten this wouldn’t happen, but it’s precisely because of the possible consequences that we have such things in place.
